subject: Runtime escape credit and integration gap analysis
messages:
From: Samira El-Hashem <samira@signalbridge.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: competitor offer + runtime assurances

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We got a formal counter from our incumbent this morning — they're offering a short-term price/credit package tied to a migration window and an operational parity run. The commercial is: 3 months free plus a $75k migration credit if we commit to a 12‑month term.

Two product asks before we can move terms forward:
- Can Redwood match a retroactive (back-dated) credit structure or do credits only apply to future usage?
- We need written assurances on KV cache behavior and a brief checklist showing what, if anything, breaks for our existing runtime (esp. multi-tenant KV cache and prefix caching for chat sessions).

I've attached our competitor sheet for context (signalbridge-econ-comparison.xlsx). Can you and your team propose a concrete alternative we can share with procurement by EOD Friday? Happy to take a 30-min call to speed this up — Mike (cc) will join for technical details.

Samira
Head of Procurement
SignalBridge

Attachment: signalbridge-econ-comparison.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Samira El-Hashem <samira@signalbridge.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, Mike Chen <mikec@signalbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: competitor offer + runtime assurances

Samira — thanks for the clarity and for sharing the sheet. Short answer up front: we can propose a bounded credit + technical validation package that preserves our SLAs and limits commercial exposure. High-level strawman below — I'll coordinate internally and get a customer-ready summary by close of business Friday.

Strawman (for discussion):
- Commercial: 10% gross MRR credit for up to 3 months applied forward to invoices (not retroactive/back‑dated) OR a one-time $50k migration credit (you pick which structures to present to procurement).
- Technical: 4-week production parity validation window (no-charge), during which we run a KV/prefix cache audit and provide a remediation plan; if critical regressions are uncovered, we agree to a rollback/fallback procedure with a 30-day remediation SLA.
- Pilot: 2-week focused pilot with sample traffic to validate latency and cache hit-rate; optional ephemeral on‑prem test if you need air‑gapped verification.

Questions for you:
1) Is the incumbent credit explicitly retroactive or does it only offset future invoices? (helps us decide forward-credit vs. one-time credit).
2) Any non-negotiables from your security/compliance side for the parity audit (e.g., access to production logs, SOC 2 evidence)?

I asked Vanessa (commercial) and Irene (deploy/eng) to weigh in on limits and risk. Can we pencil a 30-min slot today or tomorrow?

—Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Jonas,

Thanks — quick clarifications: the incumbent asked for our billing to be credited retroactively for the last invoice cycle (they explicitly called it retroactive credit), but procurement said that is a tough ask for finance. If Redwood can offer forward-applied relief plus a larger one-time migration credit that will be easier to accept.

For the parity audit: we will need read-only access to some aggregated logs (anonymized session ids OK) and a short doc listing Redwood runtimes that will be used, plus confirmation on whether their on‑prem test will require agent install or can run against our staging environment.

We have a 2‑day procurement window to include any signed term sheet if the numbers look competitive. Friday EOD is our deadline.

Samira

Subject: INTERNAL: concession matrix & risk tolerance (SignalBridge)

Team — internal notes for the external reply. Keep this narrow and visible only to procurement/legal until approved. Key points and recommended bounds: 

- Commercial guardrails:
  * One-time migration credit cap: $50k (covers uplift & engineering hours); or
  * Forward credit alternative: 20% of net-new consumption for 3 invoices (if they prefer percent structure) — note: higher than my initial 10% to be competitive but still bounded.
  * Do NOT backdate credits to past invoices — finance won't sign off.

- Technical scope (Irene to confirm):
  * Offer 4-week parity window (no-charge) + 2-week pilot with production-like traffic.
  * Provide a short checklist: required logs (anonymized), runtime images we'll use, and a small config-runbook for their infra team.
  * If we find regressions classified as "critical" (data loss, KV corruption, SLA breach), include a rollback clause and remediation credits up to $25k.

- Approval path:
  * Sales can approve up to $50k migration credit. Anything above requires manager sign-off.
  * Any on‑prem agent work must route through Solutions Eng and Security; add a 72‑hour security review SLA to the offer.

Connor: can you run a quick ballpark P&L on the two concession options (one-time $50k vs. 20% x3 invoices) so we can recommend the lower-cost path? I want numbers before external response.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Commercial GTM
Redwood Inference

Samira — thanks for the fast turnaround and the context. Per internal alignment (cc'd Vanessa and Irene), here's a concise offer you can present to procurement today: 

1) Commercial package (choose one):
   a) One-time migration credit: $50,000 applied to onboarding/first invoice; OR
   b) Forward credit: 20% credit on net-new consumption applied to the next three invoices (applies only to traffic routed to Redwood, not retroactive).

2) Technical assurances:
   - 4-week production parity validation window (no charge) during which Redwood will: run a KV/prefix cache audit, supply a remediation plan, and execute a short pilot (2 weeks) against a subset of production traffic.
   - We will supply a short checklist of required anonymized logs + runtime images. Any on‑prem agent tests are optional; they will require a 72‑hour security review and explicit SOW.

3) Risk/recovery:
   - If critical regressions are found during the parity window, Redwood will execute rollback & remediation with a remediation credit cap of $25k.

Attachments: integration-impact-notes.pdf (technical checklist and parity runbook) and the econ spreadsheet you provided are included. Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-8791 for the internal ticket and our pilot SOW template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c

Next steps: If this looks close, can procurement confirm which commercial option they prefer (one-time vs percent credit) and whether they want an on‑prem test? We can deliver a short term sheet and get legal looped within 24 hours.

Looking forward — happy to hop on a call at 4pm PT today if that helps.

—Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
